title: Per-token precision steering & zero-copy pathlets for INT8/FP8 inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: dequantization and format conversion between INT8/FP8/mixed kernels currently creates a non-trivial per-token overhead (memory copies + staging buffers) that hurts low-latency streaming and short prompt performance. We also lack a fine-grained runtime steering mechanism to choose a numeric path at token granularity when workload characteristics change mid-sequence (e.g., system messages -> user prompt -> code block -> long context).

Goal: implement a lightweight per-token precision steering mechanism plus "pathlets" (very small zero-copy kernel adapter paths) that allow the runtime to select INT8, FP8, or mixed variants on-the-fly with minimal copy tax while preserving numerical safety. This should reduce format-conversion copies, lower tail latency for short inputs, and enable smarter kernel selection driven by request metadata and observed token distributions.

Scope: prototype kernel adapters and a steering policy, integrate with kernel catalog & selector, add microbenchmarks and a gated rollout flag. Not changing model weights or quantization tables; this is strictly a serving/runtime execution layer optimization.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end P95 decode latency for 8-token prompts on c5-gpu baseline <= SLO (example: 120ms) and no more than 3% regression versus the best existing INT8 fastpath.
2) Measured copies per token reduced by >= 60% for mixed-precision traces in our microbench harness.
3) New kernel pathlets exercised by unit/integration tests with numerical validation against FP32 reference (max relative error thresholds documented).
4) Kernel selector heuristics + per-token steering enabled behind feature flag and defaulted off for Dedicated until pilot customers opt in.
5) PR with code + perf tests merged and console docs updated (link in comments).
design_notes:
- Introduce a tiny metadata header on decode requests: preferred_precision_hint (none|int8|fp8|auto), token_scope (per-token|per-chunk).
- Implement "pathlets": minimal wrapper kernels that reinterpret layout without copying when binary layouts are bit-compatible (e.g., certain INT8 packed layouts -> FP8 view) and perform in-register fast-conversion when required.
- Use a priority-ordered kernel catalog: exact-layout zero-copy pathlet -> light conversion kernel (in-register requant) -> full dequant+reformat slowpath. Selector chooses the first compatible entry.
- Add guardrails: numerical-sanity checks during canary (sampled compare to FP32) and a soft budget for number of in-flight converted tokens to bound transient memory pressure.
- Telemetry: per-token precision decisions, pathlet chosen, conversion time, and post-conversion norm deltas. Export as tags for per-route dashboards.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (prototype, 1 week): small CUDA kernel adapters that do reinterpret_cast-style zero-copy when layout-compatible; lightweight in-register conversion microkernel for single-vector requant. Add unit tests.
Phase 2 (integration, 2 weeks): hook selector logic into kernel catalog, add precision_hint header parsing, implement steering policy module that can operate per-token or per-chunk. Add synthetic microbench harnesses comparing copy counts and latency.
Phase 3 (canary/pilot, 1 week): run on internal loadgen across model set (small->large) and compare error budgets vs FP32 baseline. Add telemetry and fallback counters.
Phase 4 (rollout): gate behind runtime-1.19 flag and enable for selected customers; monitor regressions and iterate.

Deliverables: implementation PR, perf results dashboard panels, Confluence design doc, integration tests, feature flag in config.
benchmarks:
Local microbench (A100-40GB):
- Baseline INT8 fastpath (no conversion): 1.00x throughput, median decode latency 18ms for 8-token batch=1.
- Existing mixed path (copy+dequant): throughput 0.72x, median 34ms, P95 120ms.
- Prototype zero-copy pathlet (mixed trace): throughput 0.92x, median 20ms, P95 86ms.
Notes: numbers are from initial lab runs on synthetic traces; full validation required on customer-like traces. Expect further improvement after kernel fusion pass.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: numerical divergence in edge cases (rare heads or scale factors). Mitigation: sampled FP32 shadow compare with automatic rollback if norms drift beyond thresholds.
Risk: hardware layout incompatibilities leading to misaligned zero-copy attempts. Mitigation: kernel catalog will include strict layout predicates; zero-copy only used when predicates pass.
Risk: increased complexity in selector causing regressions. Mitigation: conservative default policy (only per-chunk 'auto' in initial canary) and exhaustive integration tests + perf baselining in CI.
